request.label: gap-commentary
request.system: You write short, plain, honest prose for a developer audience about the Business Central launch event. Use only the facts given. No em-dashes, no bullet lists, no headings, no hype words. Return JSON { "text": "..." } with paragraphs separated by blank lines.
request.prompt:
Write 2 short paragraphs (100 to 150 words total) of commentary on the gap between what Microsoft documented for Business Central 2026 release wave 2 and what the launch event videos actually covered. Tone: direct, a bit of humor, no em-dashes, no hype. Point at patterns (which areas got stage time, which did not, what the undocumented items have in common). Use only the lists below; do not add facts; do not enumerate everything. No headings.

Status rule: a feature is GA unless the presenters said otherwise; "(implied)" means nothing was said.
Shown but not documented (no what's new item of its own; "[in product docs]" = a how-to article on learn.microsoft.com describes it anyway):
- Approval history and audit trail in the web app (expense-agent, announced, 6 min): The web app shows tabs for draft, submitted, approved and history, and approver tabs. History lists each step with timestamps, approver and rejection reason, and tracks amount changes as part of wider approval improvements.
- Italian Subcontracting Migration app (supply-chain, GA, 6 min, in product docs): A separate app, not on AppSource, migrates legacy Italian data and is proposed only when needed. It now works in production environments.
- Integer to big integer field change (developer-tools, GA, 6 min, in product docs): A field can change from integer to big integer while keeping existing rows, aimed at entries that run out of numbers. The compiler and AppSourceCop warn about implicit conversions and overflow, but the change is allowed without copying data.
- BC-Bench code review category (developer-tools, GA, 5 min): A category tests whether AI can review AL changes against an expected comment. An LLM judge scores whether generated comments match.
- Mirroring to Microsoft Fabric (integration, preview, 4 min): Business Central data is synchronized live into OneLake through an open mirroring database. Setup is three steps: mirror database, connect, choose tables and companies.
- Public package resources (developer-tools, GA, 4 min, in product docs): Resource folders can be marked public so other apps can list and read them as JSON or text by provider app ID, without a dependency. Private resources still work with the normal functions without an app ID.
- Tax rate mismatch handling (integration, preview, 3 min): If the Business Central tax rate differs from the Shopify rate, the order is not created and a review is forced. The user keeps the Business Central rate or overrides it with the Shopify rate.
- Contamination detection (developer-tools, GA, 3 min): Models get only the repo name and bug description and must name files to modify. Only one task matched across 101 tasks and three models.
- Early install of hotfixes for Microsoft apps (admin-and-platform, GA, 3 min): Customers can install a prepared hotfix version of a Microsoft app immediately or in the next update window from the app details page. It bypasses safe deployment, so use it only when the version fixes an issue that affects the customer.
- Subcontractor prices with closest match (supply-chain, GA, 3 min, in product docs): Subcontractor prices are matched by closest match on quantity, date, task, unit of measure and variant, not lowest price. A larger order can get a higher unit price.
- Travel requests (expense-agent, announced, 3 min, in product docs): Employees request permission to spend with budget, dates and justification, and the company sees expected expenses. On approval an expense report per trip follows and receipts are assigned to it.
- BC-Bench evaluation framework (developer-tools, GA, 3 min, in product docs): A reproducible open-source framework evaluates AI coding agents on real AL tasks from real PRs and tests. It measures the impact of model, tool, instruction and agent changes.
- Legacy subcontracting pre-check (supply-chain, GA, 3 min): An action checks for open transfer and purchase orders with WIP items before disabling legacy subcontracting. The same checks run on disable.
- PTE lifecycle management in the admin center (admin-and-platform, GA, 3 min, in product docs): Upload, install and update operations are added to PTE management in the admin center, bringing full PTE lifecycle management into one place. Installs start from the apps page with an install extension button.
- Multiple scheduled PTE installs and cancel (admin-and-platform, GA, 3 min, in product docs): Several future installs can be scheduled for the same PTE, for example one version on the next minor and another on the next major update. Scheduled installs show on the app details page and can be canceled before they run.
- Tax area code and tax liable on Shopify orders and refunds (integration, preview, 2 min): Shopify orders get tax area code and tax liable fields, filled from Shopify or by AI and used when the sales document is created, and they can be overridden to skip standard mapping. The Shopify refund page gets a tax fact box and tax lines.
- Item charges on subcontracting receipts (supply-chain, GA, 2 min, in product docs): Item charges can be assigned to posted subcontracting receipt lines, including the operation line. Production order statistics show the charge in subcontractor cost.
- Install Subcontracting app from Manufacturing Setup (supply-chain, GA, 2 min): The app can be installed from Manufacturing Setup when disabling legacy subcontracting. Without legacy data no migration runs.
- Cross-environment master data management (integration, GA, 2 min): Subsidiaries in other environments of the same tenant can pull master data from the HQ company. It is built in, with no middleware or custom code, and uses the same UI as same-environment synchronization.
- Expense Agent mobile app (expense-agent, preview, 2 min, in product docs): A new mobile app for iOS and Android scans receipts, crops the background and works offline. Users accept beta conditions and need a Business Central environment that supports the Expense Agent.
- Subcontracting app (supply-chain, GA, 2 min): The Subcontracting app, released in minor update three, is pre-installed on new environments. It extends the older subcontracting that only registered that the work happened.
- Subcontracting with warehouse receipt (supply-chain, GA, 2 min, in product docs): For directed put-away locations, a subcontracting order needs a warehouse receipt. Put-away with serial numbers is created only for the last operation, otherwise output is registered.
- Review and approve tax match (integration, preview, 2 min): A review window shows the tax area, jurisdictions and taxes per shipping and product line. A red icon marks low confidence and the user approves or cancels.
- Power BI apps on Fabric (reporting-and-analytics, announced, 2 min): The Power BI apps were converted to the Fabric backend. They will come as samples or on AppSource in single- and multi-company versions.
- Updated data picker (reporting-and-analytics, GA, 2 min): The Word add-in data picker got UX improvements. It shows the company information data set next to report information.
- Export logs pushed to Fabric (integration, preview, 2 min): Synchronization logs are also written into Fabric for monitoring through the SQL endpoint.
- Run BC-Bench on your own data set (developer-tools, GA, 2 min): Partners can fork the open-source repo and use their own bug fixes, tests and PRs. Contamination should be checked for open-source repos.
- Multi-company Power BI reporting (reporting-and-analytics, announced, 2 min): Multi-company app versions show data across companies with a company filter.
- Invoicing for France (e-documents, GA, 2 min, in product docs): Invoicing for France is introduced with three new e-document formats set up on the e-document service, including e-reporting. Lifecycle events such as collected, submitted, accepted, refused and technical rejected are stored as messages linked to the invoice e-document.
- AL code review approaches (developer-tools, GA, 2 min): BC-Bench compares plain Copilot CLI, BC Quality as a plug-in and the AL review agent. The review agent focuses on security, privacy and performance and already comments on BC apps PRs.
- Expense submission and approval on mobile (expense-agent, preview, 1 min): The mobile app supports submitting expense reports and the full approver experience. Approvers review expenses, check compliance flags, override them and approve.
- Database export as an environment operation (admin-and-platform, GA, 1 min, in product docs): An export appears on the operations page with status, times, who triggered it and the error on failure. It uses the same filters and details flyout as other operations.
- Change propagation and synchronization log (integration, GA, 1 min): Source changes show in the subsidiary after about a minute. Logs and job rescheduling work as for single-environment sync.
- MCP server on/off toggle (admin-and-platform, GA, 1 min): A toggle on the Copilot and agent capabilities page activates or deactivates the MCP server as a whole.
- Create transfer order to subcontractor (supply-chain, GA, 1 min, in product docs): A Subcontracting action on the production order creates a transfer order to the subcontractor location. It holds lines for components and the transfer WIP item.
- Agentic developer loop (developer-tools, GA, 1 min): The agent plans an investigation and uses ALSP, the AL tool proxy and the Business Central MCP server for call stacks, variables and CPU profiles. The loop is understand, capture, measure, fix.
- Intent detection and agentic loop (copilot-and-agents, GA, 1 min): Copilot detects intent from the message history and iterates through tools. Tools include Business Central, work data, other agents and the web.
- Run migration by disabling legacy subcontracting (supply-chain, GA, 1 min): Disable legacy subcontracting runs the migration, restarts the session and switches application areas. Activation is blocked while unmigrated data exists.
- Initial cross-environment synchronization (integration, GA, 1 min): Start all runs default tables in a predefined order, starting with business relations and dimensions.
- AL MCP server for coding agents (developer-tools, GA, 1 min, in product docs): The AL MCP server exposes compile, publish and search to agents without VS Code. It improved pass@5 by almost 10% in BC-Bench at the cost of longer runs.

- Get clearer guidance for AL object structure (developer-tools, General availability)
- Restrict global symbol resolution to a minor version (developer-tools, General availability)
- Simplify AL extension setup and authentication in Visual Studio Code (developer-tools, General availability)
- Track AL compiler diagnostics in automated builds (developer-tools, General availability)
- Keep Shopify connections current (integration, General availability)
- Improve duplicates prevention (expense-agent, Public preview)
- Estimate your carbon footprint in Service Management (sustainability, General availability)

output.text:
Stage time went to things that demo well and file badly. BC-Bench filled several developer-tools slots, and Subcontracting got a long run of short segments, from migration to item charges. Shopify tax handling and Fabric mirroring, both preview, also had no item of their own. Many of these are in product docs anyway, so part of the gap is filing. The documented but unshown list is mostly small quality of life: recent searches in Tell Me, image previews, avatars in lists, AL MCP logging. Nobody films a log file.

The status column is messier. Dozens of Expense Agent, withholding tax and EDI items were shown without a label, while the docs say preview. Silence is not GA, so check the docs before promising a customer anything.
